subject.title: fix(workboard): release path for legacy claims without ownerId

question: For legacy Workboard claims that lack canonical ownership fields, should Doctor preserve the historical claimant when it can be mapped safely, or clear the claim as unrecoverable before normal runtime authorization resumes?
rationale: The branch establishes a new authorization meaning for historical data, but the available evidence does not establish whether legacy claim.agentId is a safe canonical owner mapping in every shipped state.

options.title: Normalize safely in Workboard Doctor
options.body: Recommended: map only demonstrably attributable legacy claims into the canonical contract and clear or report ambiguous claims, leaving runtime authorization unchanged.

options.title: Clear all incomplete legacy claims
options.body: Treat missing canonical ownership fields as unrecoverable and clear them during Doctor repair, favoring predictable recovery over preserving ambiguous ownership.

options.title: Accept runtime fallback
options.body: Keep the proposed assignee-based fallback and explicitly own its permanent authorization and compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Normalize safely in Workboard Doctor
recommendation.body: Recommended: map only demonstrably attributable legacy claims into the canonical contract and clear or report ambiguous claims, leaving runtime authorization unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence adjacent owner for the repository migration and canonical-runtime policy governing this decision.
